strategy_title: maxnreg Register Cap Backfires on Memory-Bound Pointwise Kernels
strategy_description: Capping registers via maxnreg=40 successfully raised theoretical occupancy from 31.25% to 75% and achieved occupancy from 28.81% to 70.75%, but caused a 2x slowdown (3.13ms → 5.94ms). The register cap forced register spills to local memory, as evidenced by new MemoryCacheAccessPattern warnings (only 1 of 32 bytes per sector utilized for local loads/stores), a 3.5x increase in Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction (25.66 → 90.74), a 2.4x increase in L2 Compression Input Sectors (201M → 487M), and a drop in DRAM throughput from 83.53% to 72.73%. More active warps (higher occupancy) amplified the spill traffic, overwhelming the memory subsystem. Do not apply maxnreg register capping when the kernel's actual register demand is high relative to the cap value — forced spills to local memory create strided, uncoalesced access patterns that are far more costly than the latency-hiding benefit of higher occupancy.
applicable_when: Never applicable when the kernel's natural register count significantly exceeds the cap target — spill overhead will dominate. Only consider maxnreg when the compiler's actual register usage is already near the cap (within ~10-15 registers), so spilling is minimal.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel has high natural register usage (e.g., 87 regs/thread) and the cap target is aggressively low (e.g., 40 regs/thread). The resulting local memory spills create uncoalesced strided access patterns (1 of 32 bytes per sector utilized), causing Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction to balloon (25→90 cycles) and net throughput to drop despite higher occupancy. Also avoid when the kernel is already near DRAM saturation (>80% DRAM throughput) — adding more in-flight warps via occupancy increase will not improve throughput if HBM is already the bottleneck.
framework_notes: maxnreg is a keyword argument to triton.Config() in Triton that maps to PTX .maxnreg directive / CUDA __launch_bounds__(maxThreadsPerBlock, minBlocksPerSM). In CUDA, equivalent is __launch_bounds__(block_size, min_blocks) or explicit -maxrregcount compiler flag. Both can cause register spilling if the cap is set too aggressively relative to actual kernel register demand.
